violence.10.why: Divides pacifist and canon-law traditions, where clergy and monks bear no arms, from doctrines of defensive jihad, milchemet mitzvah or total mobilisation, where every believer fights; most secular schools see no stake in clergy status and simply accept it.

notes.VEF: Defensive jihad is an individual duty (fard ayn) and Iranian clergy fought in the Iran-Iraq war: 3.
notes.RZ: Mishnah Sotah 8:7 on the obligatory war (milchemet mitzvah): even the bridegroom leaves his chamber; hesder yeshiva soldiers: 3.
notes.GAN: Satyagraha excludes arms even against invasion; no one, least of all a holy person, should bear them: -3.
notes.CA: Tolstoy and Ballou read the Sermon on the Mount as forbidding all killing, including in defence: -3.
notes.EB: Thich Nhat Hanh and Thich Quang Duc answered war with nonviolence; the Vinaya forbids monks to kill: -3.
notes.CST: Aquinas (ST II-II q.40 a.2) and Canon 285 par.3 bar clerics from bearing arms, though defence by laity is just: -2.
notes.SR: French Radicals, via the 1889 law, made seminarians do military service (cures sac au dos); no clerical exemption: 2.
notes.COR: Vendee and Carlist priests took up muskets for throne and altar: 2.
notes.BK: Vinaya forbids monks to kill or join armies though the king defends the realm: -2.
